summary: Lane County, OR lookout run by the Western Lane Fire Patrol; built 1936 per Forest Lookouts (1938 per Register); destroyed in the 1962 Columbus Day hurricane.

facts.design: Wooden L-6 tower with cabin per Register and firelookout.com; 1936 records describe a creosoted ring-connected tower with a 7 x 7 cab
facts.status_note: Destroyed in the Columbus Day hurricane on October 12, 1962; no source describes what remains at the site

staffing.status: Kenneth Fildes on detached duty as lookout, reported in August 1937; no other staffing record found

events.note: August 1934 letter to the Regional Forester: the lookout house was bought and in storage; a trail was suggested to pack it in
Construction began September 15, 1936 on a tower with a 7 x 7 cab; a foreman and crew of five finished it within about a month
Kenneth Fildes on detached duty as lookout in August 1937; the Forest Log says he reported a number of fires accurately
Register and firelookout.com date the tower to 1938; this conflicts with the 1936 construction records
One quarter mile of road built to the lookout; dwelling house refinished inside and re-roofed
Destroyed in the Columbus Day hurricane, October 12, 1962
Registered March 30, 2011 as US 912, OR 279; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and firelookout.com date the tower to 1938; the Forest Lookouts page quotes 1936 construction records (started September 15, 1936, finished within a month). The story reports both dates.
Sources give 100 feet (1936 records), 103 feet (Forest Log, November 1936) and 110 feet (Register, firelookout.com). The brief's 30.5 m (100 ft) was kept because it matches the construction record.

notes_for_editor: Build year and height disagree between sources, as noted in the story; the 1936 construction record is the most detailed. The destruction date (October 12, 1962) is consistent across all three sources. No source describes the site today, and no access information was found, so facts.access is omitted. The Forest Lookouts township note (19S-7W-14) differs from its 1936 annual report entry (section 14 T17S R6W); not used. Coordinates and elevation in the brief match the Register. Research used 1 WebSearch and about 5 page reads.
